claim: CAR (certainty-based routing) answers short first and uses long reasoning only when the short answer has high perplexity. On three text benchmarks it used about 45% fewer tokens than always-long and scored higher on average (Qwen2.5-7B 81.1 vs 75.0; Llama3.1-8B 74.9 vs 70.8).
quote: It first produces a short answer, then scores its own perplexity and only triggers long-form reasoning when confidence is low.
authors: Lu, Yu, Xu, Ran, Tang, Wang, Shan, Fu, Feng, Tang, Wang, Huang
title: Prolonged Reasoning Is Not All You Need: Certainty-Based Adaptive Routing for Efficient LLM/MLLM Reasoning
n: 3 text benchmarks (GSM8K, StrategyQA, MathQA), 2 small models
transfer: Router step: take a short answer first, measure token-level confidence, spend extra reasoning only below a threshold.

claim: CAR is not an equal-token test. It compares with always-long at each method's own token use and does not clearly count the gate overhead. On GSM8K with Llama3.1 CAR was slightly worse (71.6 vs 72.9).
authors: Lu, Yu, Xu, Ran, Tang, Wang, Shan, Fu, Feng, Tang, Wang, Huang
title: Prolonged Reasoning Is Not All You Need
transfer: When we test a gate, match total tokens including the gate, and include a gate-off arm.

claim: Confidence-gated CoT was tested with four training-free confidence measures against random gating and an oracle. Measures can cut redundant reasoning, but their usefulness is inconsistent across settings.
quote: the utility of individual confidence measures is inconsistent across settings.
authors: Lewis-Lim, Tan, Zhao, Aletras
title: Can Confidence Estimates Decide When Chain-of-Thought Is Necessary for LLMs?
transfer: Do not trust one confidence signal for the router. Use more than one and log when they disagree.

claim: SelfBudgeter trains a model to estimate its own budget and cuts math response length 61% while keeping accuracy. It needs training, so it is not a prompt-only schema step.
quote: an average response length compression of 61% on math reasoning tasks while maintaining accuracy.
authors: Li, Dong, Ma, Zhang, Jia, Sui
title: SelfBudgeter: Adaptive Token Allocation for Efficient LLM Reasoning
transfer: none for a prompt-only agent. Shows easy items need little thought.

claim: Without oracle labels, intrinsic self-correction lowers accuracy in most settings: GSM8K GPT-3.5 75.9 to 74.7, GPT-4 95.5 to 89.0, Llama-2 62.0 to 36.5; CommonSenseQA GPT-3.5 75.8 to 41.8 after two rounds.
quote: LLMs struggle to self-correct their responses without external feedback, and their performance even degrades after self-correction.
authors: Huang, Chen, Mishra, Zheng, Yu, Song, Zhou
title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
n: GSM8K, CommonSenseQA, HotpotQA; GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama-2
transfer: Revision must be gated by an outside check (code run, test, retrieval), not by the model rereading itself.

claim: At equal response count, multi-agent debate does not beat self-consistency on GSM8K with gpt-3.5: 6 responses 83.2 vs 85.3; 9 responses 83.0 vs 88.2.
quote: Multi-agent debate does not beat self-consistency when the number of responses is matched.
authors: Huang, Chen, Mishra, Zheng, Yu, Song, Zhou
title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
transfer: Spend a fixed call budget on independent samples plus a vote before debate or critique rounds. Samples are correlated, so test on our own tasks.

claim: Earlier self-correction gains used ground-truth labels to decide when to stop (GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3), so they show oracle-guided results, not true self-correction.
authors: Huang, Chen, Mishra, Zheng, Yu, Song, Zhou
title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
transfer: Never let a stop rule see the answer key in our own benchmarks.

claim: CRITIC (tool-interactive critique) beats CoT on QA and beats its own no-tool variant. The no-tool variant gains little: Text-Davinci-003 AmbigNQ F1 CoT 58.6, no-tool 58.3, CRITIC 64.9; ChatGPT HotpotQA F1 42.8, 46.1, 52.9. Toxicity barely changes without the API (0.325 to 0.339 versus 0.173 with it).
quote: Unlike these models, humans typically utilize external tools to cross-check and refine their initial content.
authors: Gou, Shao, Gong, Shen, Yang, Duan, Chen
title: CRITIC: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
n: text-davinci-003, ChatGPT, LLaMA-2; QA, GSM8K, toxicity
transfer: Tool feedback is where revision gains come from. The paper reports no token counts, so gain per token is unproven.

claim: On GSM8K, CRITIC with a code interpreter beat program-of-thought for ChatGPT (72.5 to 78.2). The no-tool variant gave 77.0 for ChatGPT but 68.3 for Text-Davinci-003, below PoT 70.1. No-tool revision on math is mixed and model dependent.
authors: Gou, Shao, Gong, Shen, Yang, Duan, Chen
title: CRITIC
transfer: Revision after code execution is the default. No-tool revision only as a cheap option, A/B tested.

claim: Chain-of-thought lowered accuracy in 3 of 6 human-psychology tasks (implicit statistical learning, face recognition, classification with exceptions). Within one model, GPT-4o fell 87.5 to 64.4 on implicit learning, Claude 3 Opus 70.7 to 62.7, Gemini 1.5 Pro 68.0 to 61.95. Claude 3.5 Sonnet rose 65.9 to 67.7.
quote: In three of these tasks, state-of-the-art models exhibit significant performance drop-offs with CoT
authors: Liu, Geng, Wu, Sucholutsky, Lombrozo, Griffiths
title: Mind Your Step (by Step): Chain-of-Thought can Reduce Performance on Tasks where Thinking Makes Humans Worse
venue: arXiv preprint 2410.21333 (v4 Jun 2025); no venue listed
transfer: For pattern-feel tasks, do not force written reasoning. Keep a direct-answer arm in the router.

claim: The 36.3 point harm figure is o1-preview against GPT-4o zero-shot on a subset, because o1 cannot switch reasoning off. Clean same-model drops are smaller: 23.1 for GPT-4o, 8.0 for Claude 3 Opus, 6.05 for Gemini 1.5 Pro, about 2 for small Llamas.
quote: o1-preview: 36.30% drop, compared against GPT-4o zero-shot
authors: Liu, Geng, Wu, Sucholutsky, Lombrozo, Griffiths
title: Mind Your Step (by Step)
transfer: Quote 23.1 (GPT-4o, same model) in design notes, not 36.3.

claim: Facial recognition: CoT cut accuracy in GPT-4o (64.0 to 51.2), Claude 3 Opus (44.0 to 29.6) and Gemini 1.5 Pro (66.0 to 54.6). Classification with exceptions needed more rounds with CoT (GPT-4o 2.9 to 12.5). One 76B open model's drop was not significant (p=0.44).
authors: Liu, Geng, Wu, Sucholutsky, Lombrozo, Griffiths
title: Mind Your Step (by Step)
transfer: Harm is task type specific.

claim: Least-to-most prompting reached at least 99% on the SCAN length split with 14 exemplars, versus 16% for chain-of-thought, on code-davinci-002. One synthetic compositional benchmark. The abstract gives no token-matched control.
quote: with an accuracy of at least 99% using just 14 exemplars
authors: Zhou, Schaerli, Hou, Wei, Scales, Wang, Schuurmans, Cui, Bousquet, Le, Chi
title: Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning in Large Language Models
transfer: Decompose into ordered subquestions only when the task is compositional and harder than the examples. Test against CoT at equal tokens.

claim: Plan-and-Solve zero-shot prompting matched 8-shot CoT on math across ten datasets. This is a wording gain over zero-shot CoT, not an equal-token test.
quote: has comparable performance with 8-shot CoT prompting on the math reasoning problem.
authors: Wang, Xu, Lan, Hu, Lan, Lee, Lim
title: Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Improving Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Reasoning by Large Language Models
transfer: A plan-first line costs few tokens. Test it as an A/B, not as settled.

claim: Raoelison, Thompson and De Neys 2020 study how cognitive capacity relates to intuitive rather than deliberate reasoning. I confirmed only title, authors, journal and DOI from Crossref, not the numbers.
authors: Raoelison, Thompson, De Neys
title: The smart intuitor: Cognitive capacity predicts intuitive rather than deliberate thinking
transfer: Possible support for trust-first with strong reasoners. Open the paper before citing a number.

claim: Ghasemi et al. 2022 ask whether logical intuitions track logic. In three experiments pseudo-valid arguments interfered with belief judgments as much as valid ones, so fast intuitions may come from surface structure. Summary is of the OSF preprint record seen through Crossref.
quote: The authors conclude that the intuitive inferences come from superficial structure rather than genuine logical intuition.
authors: Ghasemi, Handley, Howarth, Newman, Thompson
title: Logical intuition is not really about logic
transfer: A fast answer can feel right for shallow reasons, so a check needs a real test, not a feeling.

claim: CHECK: Ghasemi 2022 does not report the proportion of correct initial responses in the two-response paradigm. Its subject is logical intuition. Verdict: claim 1 in claims.jsonl should drop this source or re-source it. It keeps Bago and De Neys 2017 and Raoelison.
authors: (verdict)
title: Check of claims.jsonl claim 1
transfer: none

claim: CHECK: Does agreement or confidence decide when extra reasoning helps? Verdict: partly supported, weak. Two 2025 preprints show gating can cut tokens (CAR about 45% on small models), one finds measures inconsistent, and none matches tokens or counts gate cost. Not settled for sample agreement in a single model. Test it ourselves.
authors: (verdict)
title: Check of critique missing item 1
transfer: Run gate-on, gate-off and always-deliberate arms at equal total tokens.

claim: CHECK: Verifier-gated revision versus intrinsic self-correction. Verdict: supported for external feedback (CRITIC, Huang) in QA and math, but no source here is compute matched. Intrinsic self-correction hurts in most Huang settings. No code-specific equal-compute source found because the search budget ran out.
authors: (verdict)
title: Check of critique missing item 2
transfer: Keep revision tied to executable checks.

claim: CHECK: Mind Your Step. Verdict: confirmed that CoT lowers accuracy in some tasks within one model, but 36.3 is cross-model. Size depends on the model, and Claude 3.5 Sonnet showed no harm on implicit learning. Still a preprint. No replication or critique was found, because the search budget ran out.
authors: (verdict)
title: Check of CoT harm claim
transfer: none
